title: Android is the best and worst thing about Googlebooks
summary: Google's new Android-powered laptops offer compelling smartphone integration and app ecosystem benefits, but early testing reveals flaky connectivity, awkward file-sharing, and app-casting issues. The experience demonstrates both the promise and practical challenges of Android-to-laptop convergence.
content:
I’ve been testing two Googlebooks: this Asus model, and HP’s too.	

My first week with the new Android-powered laptops has been about as rocky as anyone's, but I've slowly learned to like them, even if love still feels a ways off. Every moment that's impressed me has been thanks to Android, whether I've been accessing a native version of a useful app or quickly checking my phone notifications from the laptop user interface.
But man, sometimes it just sucks. 
Phone connectivity is flaky, app casting is awkward, and file-sharing seems to be flat-out broken. And that's just the interaction between a Googlebook and a phone - I have a whole other set of gripes about the limitations of native Android apps on a $ …

title: No Man’s Sky is coming to the iPhone and iPad
summary: Hello Games announced No Man's Sky will launch on iOS for iPhone and iPad on October 28th with the complete game experience, including all post-launch updates and the Voyagers expansion. Multiplayer functionality will not be available in the mobile version.
content:
The No Man's Sky universe is about to get a little bit smaller - but in a good way. Hello Games announced that its long-running sci-fi exploration game will be coming to iOS, with versions for both the iPhone and iPad available starting on October 28th.
According to Hello's Sean Murray, the mobile version of the game is essentially the full No Man's Sky experience. "I guess I should say this is not No Man's Sky Lite," he wrote in a blog post. It includes all of the game's many, many updates that have come out since launch - like the gigantic Voyagers expansion from last year - and the only major features missing will be multiplayer and the  …

title: The OnePlus 16 is the company’s most interesting phone in years
summary: OnePlus launched its flagship OnePlus 16 in China with a Snapdragon 8 Elite chip, massive 9,000mAh battery, and industry-leading 185Hz OLED display. The device marks OnePlus's strongest offering in years despite the company's exit from Western markets.
content:
Today the OnePlus 16 launched in China, the company's first flagship phone since quitting both the US and European markets this summer. As luck would have it, it also looks like the company's best phone in some time.
Like most OnePlus phones, the 16 is positioned around performance, with a Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 chipset, and up to 1TB of storage and 16GB of RAM. That's backed up by an enormous 9,000mAh silicon-carbon battery, one of the biggest seen in any Android flagship yet. 100W wired and 50W wireless charging complete the power setup. 
On the display front, the phone jumps to a 185Hz OLED panel for the first time. That'll no …

title: The Fitbit Edge is for folks who don’t want to go totally screenless
summary: Google officially released the Fitbit Edge, a mid-tier fitness tracker with a 46% larger OLED display than the Charge 6, physical button, and replaceable battery. The device sits between the screenless Fitbit Air and the Pixel Watch 5 in Google's wearables lineup.
content:
The leaked specs turned out to be spot-on, but there are some neat software updates too. | Image: Google	

The Fitbit Edge may not be Google's best-kept fitness-tracking secret, but as of today, its existence is official. 
The tracker sits smack-dab between the recently launched Fitbit Air and the more powerful Google Pixel Watch 5 in the company's current wearable lineup. Basically, if you have smartwatch fatigue but don't want to give up notifications, this is Google's answer to the aging Fitbit Charge 6.

Maia 300 will start being rolled out to production in 2027, and it has been designed with efficiency in mind. title: Inside the mini factory where GM builds its EV future
summary: GM is constructing a Battery Cell Development Center in Michigan to research and prototype advanced EV battery cells aimed at dramatically reducing costs. The facility represents GM's critical push to compete in high-volume affordable electric vehicle markets.
content:
If you're driving through GM's sprawling campus in Warren, Michigan, you'd likely ignore the pair of adjacent, anonymous white buildings tucked away in the upper reaches of the 710-acre space.
Inside those buildings, which total half a million square feet together, is a massive construction project that's still in progress. Once completed, it will house GM's new Battery Cell Development Center, where the automaker is working furiously to build new prototype cells with the goal of slashing the cost of its EVs.
